blocks.name: Locating agents
blocks.definition:
Describe how paper chromatography is used to separate mixtures of soluble colourless substances, using a suitable solvent and a locating agent 
Knowledge of specific locating agents is not required

blocks.md:
- For chromatography to be useful, the chemist needs to be able to see the components move up the paper

  - This is not the case for colourless substances such as amino acids or sugars
- ***Locating agents*** can be used to see the spots

  - These are substances which react with the sample and produce a visible / coloured spot for the product(s)
- The chromatogram is treated with the agent **after** the chromatography run has been carried out, making the sample runs visible to the naked eye

blocks.name: Retention factor (Rf) values
blocks.definition: State and use the equation for Rf: Rf = distance travelled by substance/distance travelled by solvent

blocks.md:
- *R*<sub>f</sub> values are used to **identify** the components of mixtures
- The *R*<sub>f</sub> value of a particular compound is always the same

  - However, it does depend on the solvent used
  - If the solvent is changed then the *R*<sub>f</sub> value changes
- Calculating the *R*<sub>f </sub>value allows chemists to **identify unknown substances** because it can be compared with the *R*<sub>f </sub>values of known substances under the same conditions
- The retention factor, *R*<sub>f</sub>, is calculated by the equation:

- The *R*<sub>f</sub> value:

  - Is a ratio
  - Has no units
  - Will always be** less** than 1

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
A student obtained the following chromatogram when carrying out chromatography.

![Using Rf values to identify mixture components, IGCSE & GCSE Chemistry revision notes](assets/56502de7ab13-using-rf-values-to-identify-mixture-components.png)

Calculate the *R*<sub>f</sub> value of the substance.

**Answer:**

- The *R*<sub>f</sub> value of the substances in the chromatogram above can be calculated by:

  - *R*<sub>f</sub> = $\frac{\mathrm{distance} \mathrm{moved} \mathrm{by} \mathrm{substance}}{\mathrm{distance} \mathrm{moved} \mathrm{by} \mathrm{solvent}}$ = $\frac{3}{6}$ = 0.5

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
When you calculate *R*<sub>f </sub>values in exams, make sure to use your ruler carefully to measure the distance moved by the solvent and the substance, or use any scale provided on the diagram.

Mark schemes can be strict about the values accepted, so it's important to be as accurate as possible when determining these distances.
